sessionTitle: Build and ship faster with a developer-optimized Windows experience

announcements.name: WinGet developer configuration file
announcements.shortDescription: A public, forkable GitHub repo with an opinionated WinGet config that installs developer tools (Python, Node, NVM [inferred], PowerToys, Git) and applies settings like dark mode and File Explorer tweaks, removing the need to manually enable developer mode; generally available today
announcements.longDescription: A WinGet configuration file, published as a public and forkable GitHub repo, that installs developer tools through a single run rather than manual setup. It takes an opinionated approach to what developers need, installing apps like PowerToys, Python, Node, NVM [inferred], and Git, while also applying settings such as dark mode and File Explorer tweaks. It removes the need to manually turn on developer mode, and is flexible so developers can configure or add other tools. It ships by default on some newly announced devices and can also be used to set up existing devices.

announcements.name: Core utilities in Terminal
announcements.shortDescription: Linux-style core utilities (e.g. grep) now run natively in Windows Terminal, letting Unix/Mac/Linux scripts from sources like Stack Overflow or GitHub work without translation to PowerShell
announcements.longDescription: Linux-style core utilities (such as grep) are being made available to run natively in Windows Terminal. This lets developers mix systems—for example, piping PowerShell output into grep—and run scripts written for Unix, Mac, or Linux without translating them to PowerShell. Code copied from sources like Stack Overflow or GitHub will work if it uses these utilities, since they are also available on Windows.

announcements.name: WSL containers and WSLC binary
announcements.shortDescription: A built-in way to create, run, and interact with Linux containers natively on Windows, shipping with the standard WSL update and exposed as an API for use inside native applications, plus enterprise management controls
announcements.longDescription: WSL containers is a built-in way to create, run, and interact with Linux containers directly on Windows, so containers just work natively out-of-the-box for local development, AI/ML workflows, and containerized testing. It ships with the standard WSL update with no extra configuration, and includes WSLC, a binary for creating, running, and interacting with containers without third-party tools. Usage is as simple as listing containers (e.g., 'WSLC container LS'), attaching to a running container's Linux shell, and detaching when done.

announcements.name: Win UI agents and skills plugin
announcements.shortDescription: A plugin bringing skills and agents (packaging, code review, design, templates) for Win UI/Windows development to GitHub Copilot or Claude Code, reportedly saving over 70% of measurable tokens
announcements.longDescription: A new set of agents and skills for Win UI and Windows development, delivered as a plugin (called Win UI) that can be installed into GitHub Copilot or Claude Code [inferred]. The plugin includes skills and agents for tasks like packaging, code review, and design, going beyond simple markdown skills by providing tools that agents can use to develop Windows applications end to end. Through this process the team reports saving over 70% of measurable tokens, reducing the cost of using AI tools to build Windows apps.

announcements.name: WinApp CLI
announcements.shortDescription: A CLI installable via WinGet that packages apps as MSIX, runs applications with package identity, and works with frameworks like Rust without Visual Studio; previously announced earlier this year
announcements.longDescription: The WinApp CLI, announced earlier this year, is a command-line tool installable via WinGet ('winget install winapp') that lets developers and agents package applications and run them with package identity without Visual Studio. It can package an app from a folder as an MSIX or run an application directly with identity, enabling use of APIs like notifications and AI APIs. It works with existing frameworks—for example running a Rust console application—so developers can keep their current framework and extend it with Windows APIs.

announcements.name: Intelligent Terminal
announcements.shortDescription: An experimental fork of Windows Terminal with integrated agents that analyze failed commands, suggest fixes, retain context across tabs, and connect to Copilot, Claude, or other agents on a permission-based model
announcements.longDescription: The Intelligent Terminal is an experimental fork of Windows Terminal that integrates agents directly into it. When a command errors out, it can analyze what happened and suggest a fix (e.g., adding a missing force attribute), or open an attached agent view where the user can ask it to fix issues; it retains context of commands run across all tabs. It comes with Copilot built in but can connect to Claude or other agents using the same protocol, and operates on a permission-based model requiring approval to access and run commands.

announcements.name: Surface RTX Spark Dev box
announcements.shortDescription: A developer-first GPU machine with the NVIDIA RTX Spark [inferred] offering up to 1 petaflop of AI compute and 128GB of unified memory, preconfigured with the developer tools by default
announcements.longDescription: The Surface RTX Spark Dev box is a developer-first GPU machine featuring the new NVIDIA RTX Spark [inferred], providing up to 1 petaflop of AI compute and 128GB of unified memory. It comes optimized with Microsoft's developer tools already available by default. It was introduced alongside the software optimizations available to all Windows 11 devices.
